So in terms of "y variables", we have three measures: 

* cétacés observés
* nombre de groupes observés
* taille moyenne des groupes
* espèce principal

and we have two contributing variables: 

* état de mer
* effort d'échantillonage

this file is going to try and understand the relationship between these variables and how to best conceptualize our target variables.

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(viridis)
  library(ggpubr)
})

cetaces <- read.table("../jeux_de_donnees/Cetaces_Transects.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ";", dec = ".", comment.char = "#") |>
  mutate(across(c(secteur, saison, etat_mer_beaufort), as.factor), 
         presence = presence == 1)
```

# Effects of Confounding variables

## Effet of effort d'échantillonage

### Presence vs. Sampling Effort

It seems likely that there is a significant effect of sampling effort on observed cétacés and/or number of groups observed. 

```{r}
pbox <- ggplot(cetaces, aes(x=nb_groupes_observes, y=effort_km, group = nb_groupes_observes)) + 
  geom_boxplot()
pscatter <- ggplot(cetaces, aes(x=nb_groupes_observes, y=effort_km)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5)

ggarrange(pscatter, pbox, ncol=2)
```

To start, is there a significant difference in effort_km between presence and absence ? 

```{r}
ggplot(cetaces, aes(x = presence, y = effort_km, fill = presence, group = presence)) + geom_boxplot()

# Get the same stats represented by the boxplot
# cetaces |>
#   group_by(presence) |>
#   summarize(mean = mean(effort_km), sd = sd(effort_km))

# ANOVA: means of effort_km are significantly different between presence = TRUE and presence = FALSE
pa_vs_effort <- aov(effort_km ~ presence, data = cetaces)

# Verify conditions of application
# Homoscedascity of residuals : ACCEPTS
bartlett.test(residuals(pa_vs_effort) ~ presence, data = cetaces)
library(DescTools)
# LeveneTest(effort_km ~ presence, data = cetaces, center = median)
# Normality of residuals : REJECTS, however the shapiro test is known to be overly sensitive to sample sizes over a couple hundred
shapiro.test(residuals(pa_vs_effort))
# Do another check here…
plot(pa_vs_effort, which = 2)
hist(residuals(pa_vs_effort), breaks = 20)
```
Normality of residus isn't respected since the QQplot is lightly tailed. Given the large size of the dataset ANOVA is probably robust enough so that it doesnt matter, but to be safe we'll instead proceed with a Welch test.

```{r}
t.test(effort_km ~ presence, data = cetaces, var.equal = FALSE)
```
Thus we can conclude that effort_km is significantly different between presence = TRUE and presence = FALSE.

### Number of groupes vs. Sampling Effort

Now let's take a look at this at the level of the actual number of groups observed. My hypothesis is that there's a linear relationship.

```{r}
count(cetaces, nb_groupes_observes)
```

Some of the effectifs for the groups are 1 ! To avoid samples of size 1 i'm gonna reclass into groupes 0, 1-5, 5-10, 11-15, and 16-20

```{r}
count(cetaces, nb_groupes_observes)

cetaces <- cetaces |>
  mutate(amt_groupes_observes = cut(nb_groupes_observes,
    breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20),
    labels = c("aucun", "1-5", "5-10", "11-15", "16-20")))

count(cetaces, amt_groupes_observes)

bartlett.test(effort_km ~ amt_groupes_observes, data = cetaces)
```


```{r}
# Effect of sampling effort on number of groupes observed => GLM 
effort_on_numgroupes <- glm(nb_groupes_observes ~ effort_km, data = cetaces, family = poisson)
summary(effort_on_numgroupes)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(effort_on_numgroupes)
```
there is some crazy weirdness with the diagnostic plots here



# Relationship between mesured values

## Relation between num groups & average size

```{r}
ggplot(cetaces |> na.omit(), aes(x=nb_groupes_observes, y = taille_groupe_moyenne)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + 
  labs(title = "Number of groupes observed vs. average size of groups")

test <- aov(taille_groupe_moyenne ~ nb_groupes_observes, data = cetaces |> na.omit())
summary(test)
```
The ANOVA shows that there is no significant relationship between the number of groupes observed on a transect versus the average size of said group.
